notes.claim: Gauss elimination turns the equations into triangular form with the same solution, then solves by back-substitution.
Row operations on a matrix include multiplying a row by a nonzero number and adding a nonzero multiple of one row to another.
Breaking a circuit into simple loops and applying Kirchhoff's law gives linear equations in the unknown currents.
A set of equations may have a unique solution, infinitely many or none.
A power network's self and mutual admittances form its bus admittance matrix.
A reactor core code solves its core matrix with a linear system solver.
